ladakh.summary: For the Pakistani-controlled parts of Kashmir see Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir.
climate: In summer, the short growing season brings bursts of colour to the landscape, with wildflowers carpeting alpine meadows and barley fields turning golden under the clear mountain sun.
The region is home to iconic high‑altitude species such as the snow leopard, Himalayan ibex, blue sheep (bharal), and Tibetan wild ass (kiang).
Birdlife is abundant in summer, when migratory species arrive to breed in the wetlands and lakes.
Ladakh’s climate is shaped by its altitude and its position in the rain shadow of the Himalayas.
The region receives very little rainfall, making it one of the driest parts of India.
closures: Over time, Ladakh became known as “Little Tibet”, a reflection of its close cultural and religious affinity with the Tibetan world.
Snowfall is common at higher elevations, and many remote villages become inaccessible for months at a time.
Non-Ladakhi visitors will need a permit to visit remote areas close to the Chinese or Pakistani border, like Nubra Valley, Pangong Lake, and Tso Moriri.
permits: Non-Ladakhi visitors will need a permit to visit remote areas close to the Chinese or Pakistani border, like Nubra Valley, Pangong Lake, and Tso Moriri.

climate: In the late 19th and early 20th century, modern tourism began to take hold in the city, especially on and around the Dal lake, with houseboats being built to accommodate British officers and their families who came in the summers seeking respite from the heat of the plains of northern India.
Most people visit the city in the summer months.
The temperature at this time is cool to pleasant.

manali.summary: Manali is a city of about 11,000 people (2023) in Central Himachal Pradesh.
climate: It is a popular tourist spot for Indians in summer and a magical, snow-covered place in winter.

jim corbett national park.summary: Jim Corbett National Park is in the state of Uttarakhand in the Himalayan North region of India.
climate: Every season more than 70,000 visitors come to the park.

There are three well defined seasons: the winter season which lasts from November to February, the summer season which lasts from  March to June, and the rainy season which covers the rest of the months.
The summer rains cause flooding in the park.
The temperature in the winters can go down to 4 °C at night and the entire jungle is dry in the summer months as the temperature goes up to 44 °C.
The annual rainfall in the park ranges between 1400mm and 2800mm.
closures: The main areas (Dhikala and Bijrani) of Jim Corbett National Park are closed from 16 June - 14 Nov for the monsoon season.

himachal pradesh.summary: Himachal Pradesh (Hindi: हिमाचल प्रदेश, Sanskrit: हिमाचल प्रदेश) is a state in north India, and offers much for those looking to experience the Himalayas.
climate: The British were drawn to the cool climate and scenic beauty of the region, establishing Shimla as their summer capital and building hill stations such as Dalhousie, Kasauli, and Chail.

The state rises sharply from the Shivalik Hills in the south to the snow‑covered Greater Himalayas in the north, creating a landscape of deep valleys, terraced fields, dense forests, and fast‑flowing rivers.
The lower hills experience warm summers and mild winters, while the mid‑Himalayan regions enjoy cool summers and snowy winters that draw travellers seeking mountain views and winter sports.
Higher areas, especially Lahaul and Spiti, remain cold and arid for much of the year, with many passes closing during winter due to heavy snowfall.
Monsoon rains affect the southern and central regions, bringing lush greenery but also occasional landslides.

delhi.summary: Delhi (Hindi: दिल्ली Dillī, Urdu: دہلی Dihlī, Punjabi: ਦਿੱਲੀ Dilī), the largest city in northern India, is the country's thriving melting pot.

The climate in Delhi goes through five distinct seasons.
Spring, in the months of February and March, is pleasant with warm days and cool evenings.
Summer, in April and May, is uncomfortably hot with temperatures soaring as high as 45 °C.

nagpur.summary: Nagpur (Marathi: नागपूर Nāgpūr), a major city in the Indian state of Maharashtra, is famous for its Nagpur oranges and also widely considered to be the city at the center of India.

air: Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport (NAG  IATA), metro: Airport  Orange  (7 km from the city centre).
It is connected to Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Raipur, Nashik, Bangalore, Ahmedabad, Indore, Pune, Bangkok (Thailand), Sharjah (UAE), Doha (Qatar) and Dubai (UAE).
Many airlines fly into Nagpur.
rail: 2 Nagpur Junction  CR  SECR .
Nagpur can be considered the centre of India as the zero milestone of India is in the city.
It is almost equidistant from all the major metro cities.

kolkata.summary: Kolkata (Bengali: কলকাতা Kolkātā, Hindi: कोलकाता Kolkātā), formerly and still fondly called Calcutta, is the largest city in eastern India and the capital of the state of West Bengal.
climate: Kolkata has three main seasons: summer, monsoon, and winter.
Summer, from March–May, is hot and humid with temperatures touching 38-42°C.
Monsoon starts in June and lasts till September or October.
Winter is from November to February.
This is the best season to visit the city, as the weather is very pleasant with temperatures ranging between 8 and 20°.
closures: From the 1960s to the late 1990s, several factories were closed and businesses relocated.
By bus: Buses to Howrah Station stop to a bus terminal close to the Howrah Bridge.
All shops in Kolkata get closed by 10PM, except pharmacies.

air: 1 Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport (CCU  IATA, Dum Dum Airport, Kolkata Airport), Jessore Rd (about 18 km (11 mi) outside the city centre), ☏ +91 33 2511 8036, +91 33 2511 8787, +91 33 3987 4987, fax: +91 33 2511 9266, apdkolkata@aai.aero.
The airport has excellent connectivity with most of the major cities in India, including Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
It is a major centre for flights to Siliguri and North-Eastern India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Southeast Asia and the Middle Eastern cities of Dubai and Doha.
rail: Kolkata is served by five major railway stations across the metropolis, which connects the city to almost all the major stations in India.
Most local trains serving Kolkata run from Howrah and Sealdah stations.
The trains run as far as Lalgola (near Murshidabad) at the north, Hasnabad at the east, Namkhana at the south, Midnapore at the southwest and Bardhaman at the west.
road: Bankim Setu at the end of the platforms allows the cars to exit the complex quickly.
Santragachi also has a big bus terminus with bus services to various places in South Bengal.
Kolkata is well served by buses from destinations both inside and outside India.
sea: 3 Sealdah  ER  (code: SDAH), APC Rd, Sealdah.
One of the busiest railway stations in India with a huge number of people commuting to the city for work.
The station is divided into Sealdah North, Sealdah Main and Sealdah South.

darjeeling.summary: Darjeeling (Nepali: दार्जिलिङ Dārjiling, Bengali: দার্জিলিং Dārjiling) is a hill station in the northern region of West Bengal.
closures: In June 2008, a strike paralysed the area, with closed hotels, restaurants and shops, and the accompanying protests even turned violent a couple of times.

air: The nearest international airport is Bagdogra (IXB IATA) in Siliguri, 96 km from Darjeeling town.
There are flights from Bangkok, Paro and to most major cities in India.
rail: Siliguri Junction is the nearest broad-gauge station, on the main inter-city line.
From Siliguri Junction, the narrow-gauge Darjeeling Himalayan Railway completes the journey to 1 Darjeeling, with an additional stop at 2 Ghum.
Fondly known as the "Toy Train", the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway is the first, and still the most outstanding, example of a hill passenger railway.
road: Siliguri is the nearest city on the mainline rail network.
Ample transport is available to Darjeeling from here, a 3-hour drive on a well-maintained, hilly paved road.
Shared terrain vehicles depart regularly from several locations around town.

kalimpong.summary: Kalimpong (Nepali: कालिम्पोङ Kālimpong, Bengali: কালিম্পং Kālimpong) is a hill station in North Bengal, and the headquarters of the Kalimpong district of West Bengal.
climate: At around 1,250 metres, the town enjoys a moderate climate, which attracts people from towns at higher altitudes in the winter and from the Northern Plains in the summer.

air: Pakyong Airport (PYG IATA) in Sikkim is the nearest airport to Kalimpong, and the airport is connected to the town by NH 717A up to Algarah, and then SH 12.
However, it is not ideal if you can't avoid taking plastic in Sikkim, as plastic is banned in the state.
Bagdogra International Airport (IXB IATA) in Siliguri is an alternative to Pakyong, but it involves climbing uphill from the plains along NH 10.
rail: Sevoke is the nearest railhead to Kalimpong, and NH 10 up to Teesta Bazaar is the easiest way to get here from Sevoke.
road: NH 10 is the easiest way to get here from Siliguri or Gangtok, and SH 12 is useful if you come from Darjeeling town.
You can also take NH 717A if you come from Malbazar.
Kalimpong is accessible mainly by terrain vehicle, due to the winding mountain roads.

siliguri.summary: Siliguri (Bengali: শিলিগুড়ি Shiliguṛi, Hindi: सिलीगुड़ी Silīguṛī), the largest city in northern West Bengal, is a liberal and cosmopolitan city that is known for its vibrant music scene and strong youth culture.
climate: Siliguri has a warm summer, cool winters and a severe monsoon.
In summer, the temperature varies from a minimum of 18-22 °C to a maximum of 26-32 °C.
The temperature in summer sometimes exceeds 35 °C.
On the other hand, the winter maximum temperature hovers around 20-24 °C, and the minimum drops 6-9 °C.
January is the coldest month with an average temperature of 16.1 °C.

air: 1 Bagdogra International Airport (IXB  IATA), Bagdogra (14 km (8.7 mi) from the city centre), ☏ +91 353 269 8431.
The airport has links with most major Indian cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata and Guwahati.

In addition, a number of airlines operate connecting flights from Bangkok, while Druk Air offers twice in a week direct flights to the Thai capital, which begin and terminate in Paro with a stop here.
rail: Siliguri is served by four Rajdhani Express trains, two Vistadome Express trains, two Humsafar Express trains, four AC Superfast Express trains, a Shatabdi Express train, and a Vande Bharat Express train.
There's also the Mitali Express from Bangladesh.
The busiest railway station in North Bengal with connections to almost all parts of India.
road: By bus: North Bengal State Transport Corporation (NBSTC) operates bus services from NJP to Siliguri city centre.
There are private bus options as well.
By taxi: Ride-hailing services, such as Uber, Rapido and Ola, provide rides from NJP to various parts of the city.

sikkim.summary: Sikkim (Nepali: सिक्किम Sikkim; Sikkimese: སུ་ཁྱིམ་ Sikkim) in Eastern India, is a mountainous border state in the Himalayan foothills.
climate: The orchids blossom from March to May.
closures: It has been closed since June 2024.
After 44 years of closure, the Nathu La pass to Tibet, China – a part of the historic Silk Road – opened again in July 2006.
permits: An Inner Line Permit (ILP) is required and provided upon arrival for foreigners.
Obtaining a permit is a pure bureaucratic formality and usually takes a few minutes.
The permit can be obtained when crossing the Sikkim state border by road in Rangpo or Meili and from the Sikkim Tourism Centre in Siliguri located at the S.N.T.

air: The website of Ministry of Home Affairs states that permits can also be obtained at large international airports (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata), but locating the relevant facilities has proven difficult for some travellers, due to incompetence of personnel.
Sikkim's first airport at Pakyong (PYG IATA) opened in 2018, but has only sporadically seen commercial scheduled flights.
It has been closed since June 2024.
rail: means "Sikkim Nationalized Transport") in the vicinity of Siliguri Junction railway station (different from New Jalpaiguri station, and reachable from there by taxi/public shared taxi).

03592-223041) or from the police station at Mangan, Gyalshing or Namchi The Inner Line Permit allows travels in Southern Sikkim and great parts of Eastern and Western Sikkim with the exception of treks in high mountain areas.

Construction of a 50-km rail link from Sevoke, West Bengal to Rangpo, Sikkim started in 2009, but is not expected to be ready until 2019, and it'll take another few years until it reaches another 40 km to Gangtok.
road: The permit can be obtained when crossing the Sikkim state border by road in Rangpo or Meili and from the Sikkim Tourism Centre in Siliguri located at the S.N.T.
bus stand (the place from which government buses depart for Sikkim: S.N.T.

gangtok.summary: Gangtok (Nepali: गंगटोक Gaṅgṭok, Tibetan: སྒང་ཐོག་ Gangtok) is a bustling, friendly hill station, and the capital of the Himalayan state of Sikkim.
climate: The best season to visit Gangtok is Jan-March.
closures: The roads in Gangtok are not intact, and sometimes the main highway remains closed due to frequent landslides.

air: 1 Pakyong Airport (PYG  IATA) (35 km south in the town of Pakyong).
The only airport in Sikkim.
Bagdogra Airport (IXB IATA) in Siliguri is farther away, roughly 120 km from Gangtok, but offers more flight connections.
rail: The nearest train station to Gangtok is New Jalpaiguri in Siliguri which has direct connections to New Delhi, Kolkata, and other major cities in India.
It is a 10- to 12-hour journey from Kolkata.
Once you arrive in New Jalpaiguri, you can either hire a taxi from the station itself or take an auto-rickshaw to the Siliguri bus stand.
road: The roads in the area are all winding mountain roads in poor condition.
The average travel speed between Gangtok and other cities is around 30 km/h.
Shared terrain vehicles connect Gangtok to Siliguri, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, and other mountain locales.

pelling.summary: Pelling is a small town in West Sikkim.

road: Pelling is about 133 km away from Siliguri and 125 km from Gangtok and well connected by bus and jeep services.
The quickest way to get to Pelling is to take a 30 min share jeep from Geyzing which acts as the main transport hub for the area.
However, if you are sick of being crushed amongst 10 other locals then the walk along the road is particularly pleasant and it should only take around 4-6 hr.

tawang.summary: Tawang is a town in the Himalayas in the far west of the state of Arunachal Pradesh in North-Eastern India.
permits: All visitors require a permit to enter Arunachal state.

This means an Inner Line Permit (ILP) for Indians, which can be obtained online from eILP, and a Protected Area Permit (PAP) for non-Indians, which can be obtained in person from the Arunachal Bhawan in Guwahati if you're an independent traveler.
If entering by land from the direction of Tezpur, as most tourists do, you will be required to show your permit at the police checkpoint at the state border in Bhalukpong.

air: Arunachal Pradesh Government provides Helicopter services from Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati to Tawang.
The flying time from Guwahati to Tawang is 1 hour 20 minutes.
For bookings, contact sales counter of Arunachal Pradesh Civil Aviation at Guwahati Airport.
road: The highest point of the road, the Sela Pass between Dirang and Tawang, is notoriously difficult, and heavy snowfall (mostly during winter) could force you to stay on either side.
Tawang town is about a 16-hour drive from Guwahati.
The road is long and winding, rising far up into the mountains, back down again, and back up more than once.

shillong.summary: Shillong (shih-LAWNG), the capital of Meghalaya, is often called the Scotland of the East because of its rolling hills.
climate: The Assam-style houses with slanting roofs, a large number of windows, and wooden floors look like a piece of art (and happen to be very good idea, considering Shillong lies in an area where rains and earthquakes are very common).
The best time to visit is during the monsoon - most of the famous waterfalls including those in Cherrapunji are in full flow in this time of the year.
Shillong receives heavy rainfalls during monsoon and the rainy season usually lasts longer than in the rest of India.
Although people avoid the rainy season, it is generally the time when the city is clean (rains wash the streets of all garbage) and waterfalls are in full strength.

air: The government of Meghalaya operates a service to/from Guwahati Airport, and also to/from Tura.
The helicopter flies to the ALG (Advanced Landing Ground) Shillong, an Air Force Heliport located around 15 km away from the city center.
Travelling by helicopter reduces the tedious 4 hour road journey from Guwahati to a pleasant 20-minute flight.
rail: There are no rail lines in Meghalaya.
The nearest railway station is Guwahati, 105 km away (~4 hours via taxi, 500 rupees).
Guwahati is very well connected with all major cities of India.
road: The main interstate bus stand is located right next to Guwahati railway station.
Buses run by Assam State Transport Corporation (ASTC) and Meghalaya Transport Corporation (MTC) ply every half an hour from Guwahati to Shillong.
Many of the buses are very old, and the only visible difference among bus class is the number of people allowed to sit.

cherrapunji.summary: Cherrapunji (also spelled as Cherrapunjee and Charrapunji, but almost always called Sohra by locals), is a town in East Khasi Hills district in the Indian state of Meghalaya.
climate: Cherrapunji is in a dramatic location, on a plateau 600 metres above the surrounding valleys which, given the amount of rainfall, are naturally lush and full of diverse vegetation.
However, the flat area at the top has a limited water supply, and looks surprisingly desolate in the dry season.

Although Cherrapunji still receives a lot of rainfall, locals in some areas nevertheless have to walk for several kilometres for potable water and also face agricultural difficulties associated with topsoil erosion.
Cherrapunji receives both the Southwest and Northeast Monsoons, which combine to form a single monsoon season locally.
The months with the highest rainfall are June and July, followed by August, September and May, but effectively, April through October can be considered the monsoon season.

air: Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, is the nearest airport to Cherrapunji, and is accessible from Guwahati.
road: In the other direction, shared sumos and taxis to Shillong are available from Sohra Market in Upper Cherrapunji for the same price.
There may be some available from Saitsohpen village in Lower Cherrapunji as well, across the street and just uphill from the intersection with all the shops.

guwahati.summary: Guwahati (Assamese: গুৱাহাটী Guvāhāṭī), the largest city in the northeast Indian state of Assam, is the nerve centre of both the Assamese culture as well as the broader Northeast Indian culture.
climate: However, the city’s pleasant environment is somewhat offset by inadequate regional investment, evident in the lack of reliable drainage, which leads to frequent flooding during the monsoon season, as well as by low air quality.
Summers last here from April to May, monsoons from June to September and winters from October to March.
Temperatures here approximately range between 19°C and 26°C.
Humidity often reaches more than 80-90%.

air: 1 Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport (GAU  IATA, Guwahati Airport, Borjhar Airport).
The hub for domestic and limited international flights to the Northeast.
The hill stations of Shillong and Tura are connected by scheduled helicopter services run by Pawan Hans.
rail: Guwahati is well connected by train with all of India's major cities, and is served by two railway stations:
2 Guwahati  NFR  (code: GHY).
The main station, serving the city centre.
road: NH-31, NH-37 and NH-40 pass through Guwahati.
It is a 2- to 2½-hour drive via Rangia to the Bhutanese border town of Samdrup Jongkhar.
It is connected to all major cities of North-Eastern India by bus.
sea: Luxurious vessels with AC upper decks connect Guwahati to Dibrugarh, passing through Kaziranga and Tezpur.

kaziranga.summary: Kaziranga National park (Assamese: কাজিৰঙা Kājiraṅā) is in the Golaghat, Sonitpur, Biswanath and Nagaon districts of Upper Assam.
climate: Summer (April - May): Dry and windy.
Monsoon (June - September): Hot and humid.
Winter (November - February): Cool and dry.
Note: The park remains closed from May to October due to the Brahmaputra river floods.
It varies from very hot and humid in the summer (April to June) to cold nights and warm days in  thewinter (from November to January).
closures: Note: The park remains closed from May to October due to the Brahmaputra river floods.
When it rains, Kaziranga becomes inaccessible.
Most local cases of malaria occur in the summer, when the park is closed.

road: Get down at Kohora Town on Guwahati-Jorhat route.
Both air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned buses are available.
Booking can be done through Red Bus app.

puri.summary: Puri (ପୁରୀ Purī), also known as Jagannath Puri (the Abode of Lord Jagannath) or Purushottama Puri, is a seaside pilgrimage town in the Indian state of Odisha.
climate: Even weather-beaten, battle-hardened, super-immune Indian stomachs can not tolerate these tasty but unhygienic attacks on your digestive system.

air: The nearest airport is in Bhubaneswar, (60 km (37 mi)) from Puri.
Then take a train or bus to reach your destination.
rail: Puri is well-connected by railways.
Trains are available from Howrah, New Delhi, Ahmedabad, Bhubaneswar etc.
It is also a major railhead on the East Coast Railway, bifurcated from Khurda Road.

konark.summary: Konark or Konarak (Odia: 6କଣାର୍କ Koṇārka) is a small town in Coastal Odisha, on the Bay of Bengal, 65 kilometres from Bhubaneswar, famous for its 13th-century Sun Temple and the Chandrabhaga River.
climate: The entire territory lies in the tropics and hence is subject to high temperatures.
closures: Until fairly recent times, in fact, the temple was close enough to the shore to be used as a navigational point by European sailors, who referred to it as the 'Black Pagoda'.

air: The nearest airport is at Bhubaneswar (BBI IATA), which is about 64 km away.
It is linked with Kolkata, Delhi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Bangalore, and Nagpur and operates several direct flights.
rail: The railway stations nearest to Konark are in Puri and Bhubaneswar.
These stations are linked with almost all the major destinations in India by train.
road: The convenient way to get to Konark is drive either from Puri (33 km) or Bhubaneswar (65 km).
The National and State Highways link Konark with Puri and Bhubaneswar forming a virtual triangle popularly known as Golden Triangle of East.
To reach Konark from Bhubaneswar, after travelling 20 km take a left turn once you reach Pipili.

bhubaneswar.summary: Bhubaneswar (Odia: ଭୁବନେଶ୍ଵର Bhuboneshworo), the capital of Odisha, lies on the banks of the River Kuakhai which is part of the Mahanadi River delta.
climate: Also, wear cool, white clothes in the summer.

air: 1 Biju Patnaik International Airport (BBI  IATA), apdbbsr@aai.aero.
It is small but looks new and well-maintained.
It is well connected with major cities of India.
rail: Bhubaneswar is the headquarters of the East Coastal Railway (ECoR), and it is on the main line from Kolkata to Chennai.
It is well-connected to most major Indian cities.
Bhubaneswar has two long-distance railway stations, where several express trains have a stop.
road: Bhubaneswar is on the National Highway 16 (NH 16) that runs between Kolkata and Chennai.
It is 480 km from Kolkata, 445 km from Visakhapatnam, 1,225 km from Chennai, 32 km from Cuttack, 130 km from Chilika Lake (Barkul), 184 km from Gopalpur, 64 km from Konark, and 62 km from Puri.
Buses travel to and from major cities in the region, originating at Baramunda Bus Station.

bodh gaya.summary: Bodh Gaya, a city in the state of Bihar, holds immense spiritual significance as the site where Buddha Shakyamuni is said to have attained enlightenment.
climate: Like many parts of India, Bodh Gaya experiences cases of malaria and dengue, particularly during the monsoon months.
Nonetheless, it is wise to take precautions even during the dry season, as many pilgrim activities — such as meditation — are sedentary and often conducted outdoors.

air: The nearest airport is at Gaya (10 km) - Druk Air flies from Paro once a week from November to March.
Thai Airways flies to Gaya daily.
Indigo flies from several domestic destinations including Kolkata and Delhi and even far away places like Ahmedabad and Chennai.
rail: The nearest railway station to Bodh Gaya is in Gaya, approximately 16 km away.
From there, visitors can travel to Bodh Gaya by bus or by autorickshaw.
Rickshaws are widely available, making transportation convenient.
road: The road from Patna to Bodh Gaya used to be very rough and narrow, making the three-hour journey feel much longer.

However, after the  completion of four-laning of the Patna–Gaya–Dobhi section of National Highway 22, the journey from Patna to Bodh Gaya has become very smooth and the journey time has reduced to just over 2 hours.

patna.summary: Patna (Hindi: पटना Patnā, pronounced PUHT-nah), the capital of Bihar, is a bustling city in the Indian Plains with a glorious past.

air: 1 Jay Prakash Narayan Airport (PAT  IATA).
The domestic airport serving the city.
Directly connected to Delhi, Lucknow, Kolkata, Mumbai, Bengaluru,Hyderabad, Chennai, Ahmadabad, Indore and Ranchi, with daily flights to and from Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata.
rail: Long-distance trains arrive from many other major cities including Lucknow, Amritsar, Chandigarh, Vadodara, Surat, Nagpur, Pune, Raipur, Jaipur, Bhubaneswar, Puri, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Ranchi, Chennai, Bengaluru, Mysore, Hyderabad, Goa, Mangalore, Kozhikode and Kochi.
There are three railway stations serving Patna:
2 Patna Junction  ECR  (code: PNBE).
road: Patna is connected by road with all major cities of the country via (National Highway 30, 31 & 19).

Here is the list of destinations by distance from Patna:  BodhGaya (130 km), Muzaffarpur (80 km) Rajgir (103 km), Vaishali (40 km), Kolkata (535 km), Varanasi (300 km), Delhi (988 km), Ranchi (350 km), Jamshedpur (470 km), Kathmandu (373 km), Siliguri (380 km), Darjeeling (430 km), Nalanda (90 km).

sundarbans.summary: The Sundarbans National Park (SNP; Bengali: সুন্দরবন Sundorbon) is a huge littoral mangrove forest in the South 24 Parganas district of West Bengal, India.
climate: October to February — winter, cold and temperate
March to May — summer, hot and humid
June to September — the monsoon season, wet and windy
permits: The protected areas west of the national park are covered in a separate article West Sundarbans.

air: The nearest airport is Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport (CCU IATA) at Kolkata.
One may have to take other modes of transport to reach one's destination.
rail: The adjacent inhabited areas of the Sundarbans are well connected with Kolkata by roadways and railways.
Canning  is the nearest railway station to the Sundarbans.
It is 29 km (18 mi) away from Godkhali Port.
road: State Highway 3 (SH 3) is the only highway in Sundarbans National Park.
It starts from Krishnanagar and ends at Godkhali.
sea: 1 Godkhali Ferry Ghat (opposite Gosaba Island).
Gosaba is the last inhabited island towards Sajnekhali Wildlife sanctuary and Sundarban Tiger project area of Sundarban reserve forest.
The shortest route distance to Godkhali port from Kolkata is 82 km (51 mi) and 95 km (59 mi) from Kolkata Airport.

mandarmani.summary: Mandarmani (মন্দারমণি Mondārmoṇi or মান্দারমণি Māndārmoṇi) is a beach resort in the Purba Medinipur district of West Bengal.

rail: The nearest railway station is in Contai, although many Digha tourists also come to Mandarmani.
road: From Kolkata, catch a bus at Esplanade or Howrah headed for Chaulkhola, or any bus headed towards Digha.
From Chawlkhola there are cycle-rickshaws and auto-rickshaw which you can take to Dadanpatrabar and/or Mandarmoni.
You can also hire a car from Chawalkhola for Mandarmoni.

digha.summary: Digha (Bengali: দীঘা Dīghā, pronounced DEE-ghah) is one of the most popular seaside destinations in West Bengal.
climate: Summer starts in April and continues until June with a maximum temperature of 37 °C (99 °F).
Although cold wind from the sea keeps the weather pleasant in this time.
Next comes monsoon in July and lasts till the end of September.
Digha generally experiences an average rainfall with high humidity in the monsoon season.
Autumn sets in October and lasts till mid of December with an average temperature of around 25 °C (77 °F).

rail: 4 Digha  SE  (code: DGHA).
A small terminus with three platforms, and a part of the South Eastern Line of the Kolkata Suburban Railway.
You should make reservations in advance for weekends, national holidays and sessions like Durga Puja, Diwali, Christmas etc.
road: There are three bus stands in Digha:
3 SBSTC Bus Stand, New Digha.
There are frequent bus services to Digha from Kolkata, including Esplanade, Baruipur, Garia and Joka.

mumbai.summary: Mumbai (Marathi and Hindi: मुंबई Mumbaī), formerly known as Bombay, is the largest city in western India and the capital of the state of Maharashtra.
climate: Mumbai has three main seasons: summer, monsoon, and winter (AKA milder summer).
The best time to visit is during the winter between October and February.
Humidity is also less during the winter, when the climate is pleasant; the minimum temperature is 17°C and the maximum is 30–31 °C (86–88 °F).
Summer is from March to May, with highs in the low to mid 30s (roughly 80–90°F).
It is hot and humid during this time.
closures: In the 1980s, high labour costs and unrest forced the closure of many textile mills and the city went into a decline from which it started recovering only in the late 1990s.
A high-speed railway from Ahmedabad is under construction and is planned to open in 2027.

air: Mumbai has excellent connectivity with most of the major cities around the world, including New York, London, Dubai, Singapore, Hong Kong and Kuala Lumpur to name a few.
If you are flying from Europe it is generally cheaper to fly from London, and there are many frequent flights available.
All domestic sectors are linked to Mumbai, making it the second busiest hub in the country next to Delhi.
rail: Hundreds of trains arrive daily from all over India, almost all major cities have a direct connection with Mumbai.
Trains terminate at various different stations throughout the vast city, so make sure to note which station is relevant for your journey.

Main reservation offices are at Churchgate, Mumbai Central and Bandra Terminus for the Western line, and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Dadar Central and Lokmanya Tilak Terminus on the Central line.
road: National highway numbers 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 17, and the Mumbai-Pune expressway radiate from the city providing links to all parts of the country.
The road conditions are generally better than in the rest of India.
Distances from various cities to Mumbai are:
sea: Thane Creek is bustling with ferries to central Mumbai from various cities on the southern and eastern side of the creek, such as Alibag.
Ferries from Ferry Wharf also allow cheap access to islands and beaches in the vicinity of the city and Elephanta.
There are no scheduled international ferries to Mumbai, however cruise ships dock regularly.

pune.summary: Pune (Marathi: पुणे Puṇe), formerly Poona, is the second-largest city in the Indian state of Maharashtra.
climate: Pune has three distinct seasons: summer, monsoon and winter.
Summers are typically hot with maximum temperatures ranging from 35 to 42°C.
The warmest month in Pune is generally April as compared to the rest of the Deccan Plateau where it is May.
Even during the peak of summer, the air is cool and standing under a tree can give respite from the heat.
The average rainfall is approx 550 mm.

air: 1 Pune Airport (Lohagaon Air Force Base), Lohegaon (10 km (6.2 mi) from the city centre, about 30 minutes to an hour to reach, depending on traffic conditions).
The airport has excellent domestic connectivity and some international flights operate to Middle East and South East Asia.
For arrivals, there is a money exchange stand, a duty-free shop and a pre-paid taxi stall; in airside departures, there are snack stalls and a duty-free store.
rail: It serves as the gateway for the numerous hill stations in the Western Ghats.
Pune has many connections to other Indian cities by train.
Check train availability on the Indian Rail website before you go, as train timings are subject to change.
road: Pune is served by three national highways (NH) and an expressway.
NH 48 between Delhi in the north via Mumbai and Chennai via Bengaluru in the south passes through Pune.
NH 48, a part of the Golden Quadrilateral of highways connects Pune to Bengaluru also.

lonavala.summary: Lonavla or Lonavala (लोणावला Loṇāvalā) is in the Pune district of Maharashtra, India.
climate: Lonavla is a great choice for those who wish to escape the hustle and bustle, heat and humidity of India's most populous city for a few days.
closures: Lonavla and the neighbouring Khandala are the twin hill stations close to Mumbai.

air: Lohegaon Airport of Pune falls the nearest to Lonavla.
Apart from domestic airlines, it is also serviced by a few international carriers.
The nearest international airport is at Mumbai.
rail: Lonavla is easily accessible by road and by train from Mumbai and Pune which are among the nearest locations.
For train travellers, there are plenty of options: Intercity Express, Koyna Express, Deccan Express, Indrayani Express, etc.
Lonavla has its own railway station and most of the Express trains that cross the Mumbai Pune railway line halt at Lonavla.
road: The road is one of the most beautiful ways to reach Lonavla.
By car, you can use the Mumbai Pune Expressway to reach Lonavla.
You would have to take an exit at Khandala to get in.

mahabaleshwar.summary: Mahabaleshwar is located in the Satara district and is a popular weekend gateway for the residence of Pune (120 km) and Mumbai (215 km).
climate: The majority of tourist flows happen during the monsoon and winter months.

road: 1 Mahabaleshwar Bus Station.
Mahabaleshwar is easily accessible from Pune and Mumbai.
You can take a tourist bus (Volvo) from Mumbai, departing from Dadar East, Sion or Vashi.

alibaug.summary: Alibag (also spelt Alibaug) is the headquarters of the Raigad district of Maharashtra.

rail: There's no railway station in Alibag.
Pen is the nearest railway station to Alibag at a 30 km (19 mi) drive.
road: MSRTC buses should be available from various parts of Maharashtra.
If you are leaving from Mumbai, then you have an option of boarding MSRTC buses, leaving every 30 mins - 1 hr from the Mumbai Central Bus Station.
Though they might be uncomfortable, they top in terms of punctuality.
sea: There are ferries and catamarans available from the Gateway of India, Mumbai.
The journey takes 2 hours.
However, service is suspended during the rains, i.e.

nashik.summary: Nashik  (Marathi: नाशिक Nāshik) is a city in the state of Maharashtra with a population of about 2.3 million people (2023).
climate: Nashik has three distinct seasons: summer, monsoon and winter.
Summers are typically hot with maximum temperatures ranging from 35 to 42°C.
The warmest month in Nashik is generally April as compared to the rest of the Deccan where it is May.
November is normally a very pleasant month.
Even during the peak of summer, the air is cool and standing under a tree can give respite form the heat.

air: 1 Nashik Airport (ISK  IATA).
rail: 3 Nasik Road  CR  (about 10 km (6.2 mi) away from the main city).
Trains called 'Panchavati Express' and 'Godavari Express' also ply daily between Mumbai and Nashik.
Nowadays, the newly running Vande Bharat from Mumbai to Shirdi, stops here in the morning at 9 and runs back in the reverse direction at 7.30pm in the evening.
road: Nashik is 180 km (110 mi) from Mumbai (Bombay).
There are frequent buses to Nashik from Dadar in Mumbai.
It takes 4 to 5 hours by road.

goa.summary: Goa (Konkani: गोंय / Gõy, Marathi: गोवा Govā), a state on India's west coast, is a former Portuguese colony with a rich history.
climate: The best time of the year to visit Goa is mid-November to mid-February when the weather is comfortable, dry and pleasant.
And just don't get into the water at all in the off season.
The safe swimming period in Goa is November to early May.
Temperatures in winter and summer can be extreme, so do not forget sunscreen.
closures: Villages such as these are often close to the places where most tourists stay, so a quest for accommodation is not likely to be a problem.
Government offices have a five-day week (closed Saturday-Sunday).
Panjim closes early (around 8PM) each evening, and shops here could have a fairly longish siesta break (from around 13:00 to 15:30).

air: Goa can be reached by two airports, by train, and by the many buses connecting the state with cities in India (primarily Mumbai, Mangalore and Bengaluru).
Two airports serve Goa, each one having approximately the same number of airlines and destinations.
The 1 Dabolim Airport (GOI IATA), in Vasco da Gama is Goa's oldest airport, built by the Portuguese in 1955.
rail: Indian Railways connects Goa with direct train services from Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Mangalore, Kochi, Kolkata, Thiruvananthapuram, Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad.
The destination station is usually Madgaon in South Goa.
Travelling to Goa by train is a real pleasure as the route passes through greenery and many tunnels.
road: If you are travelling from Mumbai or Pune, car travel will provide you a journey through breathtaking scenery of the Konkan area.
There are bus routes from various cities, but most traffic is from Mumbai and Pune.
Due to increasing demand from the south, there has been an increase in buses and trains from Mangalore and Bengaluru.
sea: Occasional cruise services used to sail from Mumbai to Goa, but these were discontinued because of security concerns and unpredictable weather and are unlikely to resume.

panaji.summary: Panaji, also spelt Panjim, is the capital city of the tiny state of Goa in India.
closures: The counter is open from 8AM to 6PM on weekdays.

air: The nearest airports are Dabolim Airport (GOI IATA, 35 km) and Manohar International Airport (GOX IATA).
rail: The nearest railway station is 1 Karmali (IR station code: KRMI), about 10 km to the east, but many express trains do not halt there.
A more important railhead is Madgaon Junction, 45 km to the south, being the main junction on the Konkan Railway all trains stop here.
From the railway station, taxis, rickshaws and buses go to Panaji, but if you are carrying only a backpack, motorcycle taxis are a bargain, plus you get to ride on the pillion seat!
road: Panaji is connected with the state of Karnataka to the south and Maharashtra to the north by winding highways.
A wide range of buses are available.

The non air-conditioned, state transport bus, that though cheap is an interesting way to travel, if you don't mind the discomfort of a rattling bus body, rigid seats, over crowding and stopping at umpteen villages and bus depots along the route.

gokarna.summary: Gokarna is a small pilgrimage town on the coast in the Karnataka state of India.

air: The nearest airport is in Goa at Dabolim (GOI IATA).
rail: Gokarna is connected by rail through Karwar, Ankola, Hubli, Mangalore, Kumta and Margao.
The Konkan Railway and many other trains pass through Gokarna - Kumta (35 km) and Ankola (20 km) are the nearest major railway stations.
Gokarna Road (GOK) is the station nearest to the town itself, on the Konkan Railway.
road: From Bangalore, depending on the day of travel, there are anywhere from 1-4 buses operated by KSRTC.
It is a 12-hour overnight journey from Bangalore to Gokarna.
The experience taking the overnight sleeper was described as "being driven in a bouncy castle driven by the wicked witch of the west" - beware.

murudeshwar.summary: Murdeshwar is a town in Uttara Kannada region in southern India.

air: Nearest airport is Mangalore International Airport, 165 km away.
Hubli and Panaji airports are other alternatives.
rail: Murdeshwar station lies on the Konkan Railway.
Some trains from Mumbai and Mangalore stop here.
Some other prominent trains that stop at Murdeshwar are the Nethravat Express and the Matsyagandha Express.
road: Now sleeper/sitting non-AC buses are available from Bengaluru.
Murdeshwar being along the south western coast of India is connected to the National Highway 66, (NH-66)

Drive down from Goa towards Mangalore, take the right turn after Konkan Railway station at Murdeshwar and  drive down to the beach to visit the tallest Shiva Idol in the world and a towering Gopuram located on the beach.

udupi.summary: Most Indians know of Udupi not as a place, but as a category of restaurants that serve vegetarian food in the South Indian style.
climate: The weather is fairly equable throughout the year, due to the nearby Arabian sea.
Temperature ranges from 30 to 35 °C in day time and is around 25 °C at night.
Humidity is normally high most of the time.
The rainy season is from June to September.
At this time the monsoon shows its colours.

air: Mangalore International Airport (IXE IATA) is 59 km from Udupi.
The airport is well-connected with major Indian cities and a few Middle-eastern destinations.
Pre-paid taxis (non A/C) can be booked from the counter inside the arrival terminal.
rail: Konkan Railway connects Udupi to the same cities.
Rail connectivity with Bangalore is good, but travelling by road is a good option, as you are exposed to the beauty of the nature.
1 Udupi railway station (UD).
road: The road journey through Agumbe ghats is really mesmerizing.
Udupi is located right on National Highway NH-66 (formerly NH-17) connecting Kochi with Mumbai.
See Karavali#Get in about the lowdown on this route.

mangaluru.summary: Mangalore, officially Mangaluru (Kannada: ಮಂಗಳೂರು Maṅgaḷūru), in the coastal Karavali region of Karnataka, is a blend of new and old.

air: 1 Mangalore International Airport (IXE  IATA) (at Bajpe, about 20 km (12 mi) from the city centre).

There are daily flights to Mumbai, Bangalore, Goa, Kochi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Surat, Delhi and Kozhikode in the domestic terminal, and weekly/bi-weekly flights to Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Muscat, Doha, Kuwait and Bahrain in the international one.
Air India, SpiceJet and Air India Express operate flights to Mangalore.
rail: Mangalore has three major railway stations.
2 Mangalore Central  SR  (station code: MAQ), Hampankatta (at city centre).
The terminus for Mangalore-bound trains.
road: There are many bus services from Mangalore to all the nearby towns in Karnataka and Kerala.

The long-distance bus services to major cities like Bangalore, Mumbai, Hubli-Dharwad and Goa run along the national highways radiating to the north, south and east, like NH 17 towards Goa and Mumbai, and NH 48 towards Bangalore and Kerala.
There are two bus stands in Mangalore for long-distance bus services:

bengaluru.summary: Bengaluru (Kannada: ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು Bengaḷūru), formerly Bangalore, is the largest city in southern India and the capital of the state of Karnataka.
climate: Unlike the major cities of India which are extremely hot in the summer months, Bengaluru enjoys a relatively mild climate all year round.
Summer – February to May (peak temperature is during April and May)
Monsoon – June to October (the heaviest rains are typically between June and August)
Winter – November to January (with January being the coldest month)
Summer temperatures can reach 35 °C (95 °F) and early morning temperatures in the winter hover around 15 °C (59 °F).
closures: An important stop owing to proximity of IT companies and the ring road just passing close to the station and well connected by buses to major parts.

air: 1 Kempegowda International Airport (BLR IATA), Devanahalli (40 km (25 mi) from Central Bengaluru (Mahatma Gandhi Road) and 30 km (19 mi) from KSR Bengaluru City railway station), ☏ +91 80 6678-2255, +91 80 6678-2251, toll-free:  +1 800 425 4425, feedback@bialairport.com.
The airport is occasionally subject to operational restrictions due to fog from 15 November to 15 February between 3AM-8:30AM (IST).
Flight delays and diversions may occur on some mornings due to the morning fog.
rail: Bookings can be done at either the railway stations or at the Indian Railways booking counters in major commercial and residential areas.
Booking can also be done online.
As with all Indian railway travel, have some patience for delays.
road: If you have difficulty arranging a plane or railway ticket to/from your next destination, or you prefer a little more adventure, you can go by bus.
Government and private buses run services to/from major cities like Mumbai, Goa, Chennai, Mangalore, Coimbatore, Madurai, Tirupati, Hyderabad, etc.
Buses can be a regular service with only seats and no A/C, a normal luxury bus, a Volvo A/C bus or a sleeper bus for night travel.

mysuru.summary: Mysore or Mysuru (ಮೈಸೂರು Maisūru) is the second-largest city of the Indian state of Karnataka after Bengaluru.
climate: Mysore has a tropical savanna climate with three main seasons - summer (March to May), the monsoon (June to October), and winter (November to February).
Temperatures are generally warm year-round, with average highs ranging from about 28 degree Celsius in the coolest months to a high of 35 degree Celsius in April, the hottest month.
The city experiences moderate to heavy rainfall during the monsoon season [1].

air: 1 Mysore Airport (MYQ  IATA) (10 km south of the city centre).
Mysore has its own airport.
Commercial scheduled passenger service has been on and off since the airport's refurbishment in 2010.
rail: 2 Mysuru Junction  SWR  is the city's main station, and daily trains are plying the route to Bengaluru.
Mysore is well connected to Bengaluru, with about 18 pairs of trains plying between them daily.

The fastest and possibly the most comfortable way to travel between Mysore and Chennai is by the Vande Bharat Express, which covers the Mysore–Bengaluru leg of the journey in about 2 hours, and the Mysore–Chennai section in 6:30 hours.
road: Buses run every 5 minutes from Bengaluru.
There is a choice of air-conditioned and ordinary vehicles constantly available, so finding a bus with seats is never a problem.
KSRTC also runs Flybus (Volvo Air conditioned buses) between Kempegowda International Airport and Mysore Bus Stand.

coorg.summary: Kodagu, also called Coorg, is a district in Karnataka State.
climate: If you are visiting Coorg in wet weather seasons, beware of leeches especially while walking through wet grass and in bathrooms/toilets.

air: The nearest airport and railway station is Mysore, some 100 km away.
Mangalore International Airport is the nearest airport to Kodagu district.
road: But buses are frequent and connect Kodagu to nearby Karnataka cities such as Mysore and Mangalore, among others.
The bus journey is about 4-5 hours away.

chikmagalur.summary: Chikmagalur, officially Chikkamagaluru (ಚಿಕ್ಕಮಗಳೂರು Cikkamagaḷūru), is a city in Karnataka, known for its coffee plantations and Bababudan Giri ranges.

air: Mangalore airport (IXE IATA), 170 km Bengaluru airport (BLR IATA), 250 km.
rail: Passenger trains are available from Shimoga and Kadur at a distance of 40 km.
road: Chikmagalur is on the highway from Hassan towards Sringeri and has regular luxury as well as ordinary buses from Bengaluru.
Regular ordinary buses connect Chikmagalur to Mysore, Hassan with a single services to Kozhikode.
Buses from interior Karnataka towards Mangalore too pass via Chikmagalur and hence, ordinary buses connect the town regularly to Dharmasthala, Mangalore, Shimoga, Davanagere and Sringeri.

hampi.summary: Hampi, in the state of Karnataka, India,  is the site of the once-magnificent capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
climate: Hampi hosts the 'Hampi Utsav' (literally 'Hampi Festival') every year during the first week of November.
Avoid travelling to Hampi during the months of April and May, as temperature can get as high as 43°C (110°F).
If you are planning to visit it during summer, remember to carry sufficient water so as to avoid the risk of dehydration.

air: The closest airport is Vidyanagar Airport (VDY  IATA also known as Jindal Vijaynagar Airport), about 35 km to the east, near the village of Toranagallu.
Bengaluru is the nearest international airport, 350 km away from Hampi.
rail: The nearest railway station is Hosapete Junction (code: HPT), 13 km away.
Overnight trains run several times a week from Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Goa.
You can also catch an overnight train from Mysore to Hubli and from there to Hospet/Hampi.
road: Bengaluru: 350 km; drive the 200 km till Chitradurga (featuring a fort from 10th century AD and a dam from 1907) on NH-4, take a right turn on NH-13 towards Sholapur till Hospet, and then drive another 13 km to reach Hampi (direction towards Hampi is well marked).
The road is in excellent condition till Chitradurga but then deteriorates rapidly.
You are also likely to encounter traffic jams due to ore-laden trucks plying on NH-13.

badami.summary: Badami (Kannada: ಬದಾಮಿ), formerly Vatapi, is a city in the Bagalkot district of Northern Karnataka, in Southern India.
climate: Summer months of March, April, May are hot.

rail: There is a small station in Badami, 5 km from the centre.
Trains from Bengaluru, Bijapur and other cities stop there regularly.
From the station, there are many rickshaws to reach the centre.
road: The bus stand is in the centre of the town.
There are buses for Gadag, Bijapur, Bengaluru and Hospet.
The NWKRTC bus service is very efficient.

kerala.summary: Kerala, officially Keralam (Malayalam: കേരളം Kēraḷaṁ, keh-ruh-lluhm), is known as a tropical paradise of waving palms and wide, sandy beaches.
climate: Abundant rainfall means that lush greenery lingers pretty much throughout the year.
November 1 is celebrated as Keralappiravi (Birth of Kerala) Day (also observed as Malayalam Divasam or Malayalam Day).
Kerala experiences heavy rains almost throughout the year, and is one of the wettest areas on Earth.
Kerala has three distinct seasons:
Summer lasts from mid-February to mid-May.
closures: Kerala, being close to the equator, has a tropical climate.
Unlike other parts of India, Muslims were given high-profile rankings in Kerala society by ruling Hindu Rajas and many of them are placed as close companions of ruling elite.

The most likely problems are strikes, protest processions and hartals (which are called "voluntary closure of activities" as protests, but are enforced on everyone by the organisers) which are common in Kerala, considering its highly politicised and socialist leanings.

air: There are four airports in Kerala, with flights to domestic and international destinations: Kannur Kochi (Cochin), Kozhikode (Calicut), and Thiruvananthapuram.
The airports have several carriers operating international flights.

Cochin International Airport (COK IATA) is the largest airport in the state, as well as the first Indian airport with solar-powered operations, with regular flight connections to most parts of India, of the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Sri Lanka and the Maldives.
rail: Indian Railways operates several trains to, from and within Kerala.
Trains into Kerala start from neighbouring states like Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
Long-haul direct train services from cities like Delhi and Mumbai are also available.
road: Inter-state private and government buses operate between neighbouring states.
Usually, the journey is performed at night to escape the heat of the day.
The most common inter-state bus is Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC-Karnataka) with daily buses from most major cities of Kerala to Bengaluru, Mysore and Mangalore.
sea: Kochi is a major cruise port and a large international cruise terminal is under construction.
Once completed, regular cruises will operate from Kochi.
A regular luxury cruise between Colombo, Male and Kochi is now operational.

kochi.summary: Kochi (Malayalam: കൊച്ചി Kōcci), formerly Cochin, is a cosmopolitan city in Kerala (Keralam) with a bustling commercial port.
climate: Daytime temperatures range between 30°C and 35°C and around 24°C at night.
Kochi is one of the first places to experience the heavy monsoon showers, which start around mid-May.
It thus experiences heavy rainfall between mid-May and the first week in September.
Daytime temperatures during the monsoon fall to between 25°C and 30°C.
From September to early February, the weather is fine, marked with cool winds and light showers.
closures: Depending upon the season and day bookings may close up to several days prior to departure with all remaining travellers going onto a waiting list.

air: As the financial capital of Kerala, Kochi is well-connected by air, road, rail and ferry from others parts of India, and to some other international destinations.

1 Cochin International Airport (COK  IATA), Nedumbassery (29 km from the city centre), ☏ +91 484 305-3000, +91 484 261-0115, +91 484 261-1322, +91 484 261-0033 (flight status and airline desk transfer).
The largest airport in Kerala and one of the major gateways to India.
rail: Kochi is well connected by train from all parts of India.
Most Kerala-bound trains have a major stop here.
There are two major rail terminals inside the city limits.
road: Kochi is accessible from all southern parts of the country as well as other parts of the state, through the extensive state run Kerala Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) bus services and services of neighbouring state transport corporations.
KSRTC operates 3 types of services; Super Fast (No Frills), Express (Standard non-A/C) and Garuda Hi-tech (Volvo premium).

Karnataka State buses run daily services from Bengaluru, Mysore and Mangalore with three types of services; the Rajahamsa (executive service and reclining seats), the Airavat (A/C service, with reclining semi-sleeper seats), and Ambaari (A/C sleeper service).
sea: Kochi can be reached by sea in yachts or the occasional cruise ship from Goa, Mumbai, Lakshadweep, Colombo and Male.
Almost all leading international cruises on global voyages operate to Kochi from the US and Europe at Wellingdon Island Cruise Berth.
Yachts can be anchored at Kochi International Marina or Yacht Club Marina.

munnar.summary: Munnar is a hill station in the Indian state of Kerala.
climate: Munnar is a hill station at an elevation of 1,600 m, and was a summer resort for the British during the British Raj.
You can also find gaur, langur, lion-tailed macaque, and elephants depending on the season and time of travel.
The season between October and March (post-monsoon) is considered the best to visit Munnar.
Take a rain coat with you from April to November.
The temperature in the afternoon reaches about 22 to 26 °C throughout the year.

air: Cochin International Airport (COK IATA), also known as Nedumbassery Airport.
It is approximately 125 km away from the Munnar by road.
Taxi services are easily available from airport to Munnar.
rail: The nearest railway station is Aluva, 110 km.
Ernakulam is 130 km and Madurai is 135 km.
Angamali Railway Station is another nearest rail-head to reach Munnar.
road: 1 Munnar bus stand (It is on the main street, Main Bazaar).
From this stop buses take the southern road to Adimali/Anachal/Ernakulam.
Other buses take the south-eastern road to Poopara/Theni.

alleppey.summary: The city of  Alappuzha,  also known as Alleppey, is situated in Kerala.
climate: Alappuzha, and Kerala in general, has excellent weather due to its proximity to the ocean.
The temperature rarely goes above 35 °C and never below 20 °C.
The best time to visit is from September to March.
The monsoon, from June to August, always brings heavy wind and rains.
This is an excellent time to visit if you want to partake in a bit of monsoon tourism.

air: Cochin International Airport (COK IATA).
This is the nearest airport.
You can take a taxi to get from Cochin airport to Cochin, and then a bus or train to Alappuzha.
rail: Train service is available to Alappuzha from different parts of Kerala such as Kochi (Cochin), Thiruvananthapuram, and Kozhikode, and from other major cities in India such as Chennai, Bengaluru (Bangalore), Coimbatore, Mumbai (Bombay), New Delhi, Mangalore, and Kolkata.
If you are coming from Hyderabad, you can take the Sabari Express.
1 Alappuzha railway station (ആലപ്പുഴ തീവണ്ടി നിലയം).
road: 2 Alappuzha KSRTC bus stand.
There are no buses from the KSRTC bus station straight to the beach (around Vijay Park).
3 Alappuzha private bus stand.

kumarakom.summary: Kumarakom is a tourist village in Kerala in India.
climate: With the onset of the monsoon rains, some time around June, the little streams and lagoons break their flow beds and irrigate the fertile land to an overwhelming cover of green.
Kumarakom enjoys a well-balanced tropical climate.The lowest and highest temperatures recorded are 60.8 °F (16.0 °C) and 100 °F (38 °C).
There is always a cool, fresh breeze, which makes even the warmest weather readily agreeable after sundown.
The South West monsoon is from early June to early August.
However, slight drizzles persist till early November.

air: via Cochin International Airport (75 km)
road: It is approximately 2 hours from the Cochin International Airport.
Buses and taxis are easily available at all times of the day from Kottayam and Cochin.
sea: From Muhamma (near Alappuzha) to Kumarakom Jetty.

varkala.summary: Varkala is a town in the Indian state of Kerala, about 50 km north of Thiruvananthapuram and is home of the popular Papanasam Beach.
climate: The best times to go, are of course in the season, when the beach extends out all around the cliff face for 500 m.
In the off season it's really mellow and relaxed, swim and sleep and chill out.
Only in December does it get really busy and prices start rocketing till January/February, when it starts to quieten down.
The main season runs from Dec 1st- March 31st, with December & early January experiencing the biggest rush.
If you want to go out of season, then you can stay very cheaply and of course avoid the crowd.

air: The nearest airport is Trivandrum International Airport (50 km, 1 hr 15 min drive).
rail: Varkala is also connected by the rail network.
If coming from Thiruvananthapuram and Kochi, the better option will be coming by train.
Almost all trains passing by stops at Varkala.
road: Varkala is linked by state and national highways to all the major cities in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
State Transport Buses are available from Trivandrum.
Bus service available from Varkala to many parts of South Kerala and Kanyakumari

kovalam.summary: Kovalam (കോവളം Kōvaḷaṁ), a fishing village in southern Kerala, is famous for its beaches, among the most pristine in India.

air: Advice being if they are trying to rip you off go to leave for another rickshaw and they will often back down and offer you a fair price; if not, get in a different rickshaw.
rail: 1 Neyyattinkara  SR  (8 km (5.0 mi) from Kovalam).
If you're landing at Kochuveli station, you can take AC bus from right outside the station to Thiruvananthapuram East Fort bus stop.
road: Buses to Thiruvananthapuram can also be caught from Kovalam Junction as well as Ambassador taxis and Autos to pretty much anywhere.
