When asked where you want to go, say Hawa Beach, Leela Beach/Main Beach or Lighthouse Beach in Kovalam.

thiruvananthapuram.summary: Near the southern tip of mainland India, Thiruvananthapuram (Malayalam: തിരുവനന്തപുരം Tiruvanantapuraṁ), formerly and often still known as Trivandrum, is the capital city of Kerala in Southern India.
climate: The city has a tropical climate with little temperature difference between seasons.
The mean maximum temperature is 34°C and the mean minimum temperature is 21°C.
Humidity is high, and rises to about 90% during the monsoon season.
Thiruvananthapuram is the first city along the path of the south-west monsoon and gets its first showers in early June.
However, pre-monsoon showers are common in April and May, accounting for about 350 mm (14 in) on average.
closures: Most shops close by that time.

air: 1 Thiruvananthapuram International Airport (Trivandrum Airport, TRV  IATA).
One of the few privately-owned airports in India.
It has direct flights from the Middle East, Singapore, Malaysia, Maldives, and Sri Lanka, as well as seasonal charter flights to Russia, the UK and less frequently to other parts of Europe.
rail: 2 Thiruvananthapuram Central  SR .
One of the largest railway stations in South India.
Almost all trains on west coast and bound to Kerala start & end their journey here as the station is a terminus.
road: A long-distance bus station is located diagonally opposite the railway station.
Buses ply to all major towns and villages in the state in addition to big cities like Kochi, Bengaluru, Kozhikode, Coimbatore, Tirunelveli and Chennai.
Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) operates 6 class of services, connecting to southern Tamil-Nadu cities, town and all manner of country side in Kerala.

wayanad.summary: Wayanad  is a beautiful mountainous district in the Malabar region of  Kerala located on the western ghats.
closures: Be careful and keep your car windows closed, and food items hidden.

air: The district has neither an airport nor railway lines, so the only way to get in is by road.
The nearest airport and railway stations are located at Kozhikode, around 100km away.
Bangalore and Mysore are the other two nearby cities with airports, Of the two, Bangalore is the more realistic option as there are few flights to Mysore at the moment.
road: Driving in from Karnataka via Mysore or Madikeri is easier than from other districts of Kerala, Access from Kerala is difficult because of the mountain passes or 'ghat roads'.
Buses are available from Kozhikode and Mysore.
256 km (good roads with too many humps inside the forest.

thekkady.summary: Thekkady (Idukki district, Kerala, India) is the location of the Periyar National Park.

road: Thekkady is enchanting as the road winds through tranquil countryside, rich plantations and thick jungles.
Madurai to Kumily is around 120 km (approx 4 hours in state transport bus which are available at Madurai).
sea: The sanctuary, 60 km from Idukki, 190 km from Cochin and 114 km away from Kottayam is open throughout the year, but the best season for a visit is from September to March.

kanyakumari.summary: Kanyakumari or Kanniyakumari (Tamil: கன்னியாகுமரி Kanniyāgumāri) is a town on the southernmost tip of the mainland of India, in the state of Tamil Nadu.

air: Thiruvananthapuram (TRV IATA) of neighbouring state Kerala (Keralam), is the nearest international airport, with direct flights from the Middle East, Singapore, Maldives and Sri Lanka.
And is served by Air-India, among others.
From there it takes about three hours by train or bus or taxi.
rail: Very well connected and served by rail to all major cities in India like Chennai, Thiruvananthapuram, Kochi, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata and Coimbatore.
And from here starts the second longest train route of India, Kanyakumari to Dibrugarh and Katra
1 Kanyakumari railway station.
road: Buses are frequently available from Nagercoil, the closest major transport hub.
Long-distance buses are available from Chennai, Coimbatore, Madurai, Bengaluru etc.

madurai.summary: Madurai (Tamil: மதுரை), formerly Madura, is the third-largest city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
climate: Madurai is famous for the Chithrai Festival which takes place during mid April–May, during the Hindu month of Chithrai, when millions pour into the city for the carnival.
Madurai is also famous for its yearly bull run "Jallikattu" which coincides with Pongal festival in the month of January.

air: Main modes of transport for travelers are by air and by train.
1 Madurai Airport (IXM  IATA).
served by domestic airlines and international airlines including Air India, Air India Express & SpiceJet.
rail: Trains are the major mode of entry into the city.
2 Madurai Junction railway station (Tamil: மதுரை சந்திப்பு தொடருந்து நிலையம்) is centrally located and many facilities are accessible from there.
Madurai is well connected by trains to many parts of India like Chennai, Bangalore, Mumbai (Bombay), and Delhi.
road: Madurai is served by National Highways NH-7, NH-45B, NH-49.
Almost all of them are being upgraded to multi-lane ways as part of a national highway development program.
Travel from Chennai and Bangalore will take approximately 8-10 hours.
sea: Madurai is inland, and the Vaigai River which used to be overflowing with water is now dry.
However, the nearest ports for entry are Chennai (450 km) and Tuticorin (160 km).

rameswaram.summary: Rameswaram (இராமேசுவரம் Irāmējuvaram) is a town on Pamban Island, in Southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.

air: The nearest airport is in Madurai and is 174 km from Rameswaram.
Most of the major Indian cities have daily flights here.
rail: Rameswaram [RMM] is directly connected via daily trains from Madurai, Tiruchirappalli and Chennai.
Direct connectivity from Coimbatore and Kanyakumari is available but not daily.
You might find it difficult to find a direct train from North Indian cities.
road: Connected with all important towns of Tamil Nadu, City Buses are available including night services.
Point-to-Point services, Tourist taxis, auto/cycle rickshaws and horse carts are also available.
Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) operates Rameswaram – Tirupathi daily service.

ooty.summary: Ooty, short for Ootacamund and officially Udhagamandalam (Tamil: உதகமண்டலம் Udagamaṇḍalam), is a popular hill resort in the state of Tamil Nadu in Southern India.
climate: It was turned into a hill station in the 19th century by the British, and served as the summer headquarters of the Madras Presidency.
closures: This road is closed at night as it passes through the jungle, requiring a few hours spent at the check post which is closed at night.
permits: Many portions of the hills are preserved as natural reserve forests, and special permits will be needed to camp in noncamp sites.

air: The nearby airports are located in:
rail: 1 Udagamandalam  SR  (UAM).
The Nilgiri Mountain Railway (NMR) connects Ooty with Mettupalayam.
It is a meter-gauge railway, popularly known as the toy train.
road: Ooty is well connected by bus.
Direct buses from Coimbatore take 4 hours and are operated by KSRTC (Kerala) and by private bus companies.
The private bus operators should depart from Mettupalayam Bus Stand in Coimbatore, but check it beforehand.

kodaikanal.summary: Kodaikanal  is a hill station in the Palani Hill Range.
climate: In Tamil, Kanal means "forest", but Kodai, or Kodi can be pronounced differently and could mean "the end", denote a "creeper", mean "summer" or "gift".
Unique to the Western Ghats, the Kurinji Flower is in full bloom around December once in 12 years, and it bathes the valley in a beautiful sea of blue.
closures: Another railway station that is quite close is Dindigul Railway Station.

air: The closest airports to Kodaikanal are Tiruchirappalli 150 km, Madurai 120 km and Coimbatore 175 km.
You can get regular flights from Mumbai, Tiruchirappalli, Bangalore and Chennai.
From any of these airports you can hire a private taxi, cab or take train and bus to reach Kodaikanal.
rail: The nearest railway station is Kodai Road, at a distance of 100 km.
From Kodai Road station, one can travel only by road.
Taxis are available for hire up to Kodaikanal but since these might be the only mode of transport here, the prices are often not negotiable.
road: From Dindigul city, Kodaikanal is located at a distance of 90 km approximately and there are plenty of buses plying from various parts of the state.
Buses ply from Chennai, Pondicherry, Tiruchirappalli, Madurai, Dindigul, Palani and Coimbatore.
Buses are available from Madurai (Arapalayam) to Kodaikanal at regular timings.

coimbatore.summary: Coimbatore (Tamil: கோயம்புத்தூர் Kōyambuttur), also known as Kovai (கோவை Kōvai), is an industrial city of 2 million people (2020) in Tamil Nadu, often likened to being the Manchester or Detroit of Southern India.
climate: Coimbatore is known for its various industries, engineering goods, textile mills, educational institutions, health care facilities, pleasant weather, friendly culture and hospitality.
The city has pleasant, moderate weather throughout the year, with the exception of summer, and so, is similar to a resort town.

air: The city has a civil airport at Peelamedu and an Air Force base at Sulur.
1 Coimbatore International Airport (CJB  IATA) (approximately 7 km from the centre of the city, connected mainly by the airport's own prepaid cabs).
The airport has two operational terminals: one for departure and one for arrival.
rail: Broad-gauge trains connect it to all parts of India.
2 Coimbatore Junction (CBE).
The major station in the city, well connected by trains from Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, New Delhi and Thiruvananthapuram.
road: The city has six major arterial roads and three National Highways, NH-47 (Kanyakumari–Salem), NH-67 (Nagapattinam–Ooty) and NH-209 (Bangalore–Dindigul) passing through the city.
There are four major bus stations in Coimbatore from where bus services are available from all major places in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Pondicherry and Andhra Pradesh.
All bus stations are inter-connected with local bus services throughout the day.

chennai.summary: Chennai (Tamil: சென்னை), formerly Madras (மெட்ராஸ் Meḍrās), is the largest coastal city in southern India and the capital of the state of Tamil Nadu.
climate: The company purchased the land from the local Nayak or chieftain on 22 August 1639, which is why Chennai nowadays celebrates its birthday every year on 22 August.
Chennai reflects its traditional heritage from December to January during the height of the music festival.
The Chennai Music Festival The compositions of these maestros are frequently played by today's artists during the music festival season.
The Chennai Music Festival from mid-December to mid-January commemorates the classical music of South India, including these maestros.
Its coastal position and closeness to the equator makes Chennai's climate humid and tropical all year round.
closures: Keep your doors and windows shut and locked at night and do not carry or display large amounts of cash if possible.

air: 1 Chennai International Airport (MAA  IATA), GST Rd (about 19 km (12 mi) south-west from city centre), ☏ +91 44 2256 0551.
The fourth-busiest in India (after Delhi-IGI, Mumbai-Shivaji and Bengaluru).
All international flights arrive at Terminal 2, whereas domestic flights arrive at Terminals 1 and 4.
rail: 2 Tirusulam  S  SW  (code: TLM), GST Rd (directly across the road from Terminal 2.
Cross the road by subway (underpass) and walk through the car park.).
This is the most affordable option for getting into the city centre.
road: Use the prepaid taxi to reach the central business district.
Every terminal has many taxi booths when you leave the airport.
The fares differ for the international and domestic terminals though the terminals are next to each other.

mahabalipuram.summary: Mamallapuram (மாமல்லபுரம் Māmallaburam), also known as Mahabalipuram, is a tourist town 60 km south of Chennai on the east coast of India, famous for its stone carvings.
closures: At one time you could see the Bay of Bengal almost all the way to M'puram, but now there is so much development that the ocean is glimpsed only as you get close to M'puram.
Most restaurants close by 11PM and the town is basically dead after that.
permits: Don't wander into restricted areas.

road: Buses arrive in the centre of town from CMBT and Tiruvanmiyur in Chennai and from Kanchipuram.
There are direct buses from CMBT, but you can take any bus that has ECR written on the front.
To get to the ECR from Triplicane, walk to Kamarajar Promenade running parallel with the beach.

puducherry.summary: Pondicherry (Tamil: புதுச்சேரி Putucceri, French: Pondichéry), also known as Puducherry or Pondy, is a city in Southern India.

air: 2 Puducherry Airport (PNY  IATA).
Pondicherry has an airport with facilities for the landing of small aircraft like Dorniers and Cessnas.
SpiceJet operates daily flights from Hyderabad (with connections from other major Indian cities).
rail: Auto-rickshaws are available from outside the bus station.

Nearly all cities in Tamil Nadu are connected to Pondicherry through cheap government buses that will stop at smaller towns and villages, though no centralized timetable exists and departure times and routes must be obtained from the nearest bus station to where you are.
1 Puducherry  SR  (Pondicherry), South Blvd.
road: Pondicherry is well connected from all sides.
Chennai is 160 km north of the city.
You can also hire a taxi from Chennai International Airport (MAA IATA).
sea: You can be sure of getting a seat on the bus only if you board it from CMBT in Koyambedu, which is the main bus terminus in Chennai.

hyderabad.summary: Hyderabad, (Telugu: హైదరాబాద్ Haidarābād, Urdu: حیدر آباد Haidar Ābād), the "Pearl City", is the capital of the state of Telangana.
climate: The best time to visit the city is from mid-November to mid-February.
Temperatures are mild with abundant sunshine during this time and average temperatures range from a low of 15 °C (59 °F) to a high of 29 °C (84 °F).
March to June is hot and dry with occasional thunderstorms.
Highs can reach 45 °C (113 °F) or more and a lack of air-conditioning can make it feel very uncomfortable.
July, August, September and October can be quite warm and humid.
closures: It is far from the city, and with the exception of Novotel, there aren't any good hotels close by.

air: 1 Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (HYD  IATA), Shamshabad (22 km (14 mi) from the city centre), ☏ +91-40-66546370, rgia.customersupport@gmrgroup.in.
The sleek and well-organised airport is one of the best in India.
As you would expect from a major international airport, there is good domestic as well as international connectivity from many locations.
rail: There are three major railway stations serving Hyderabad, and as these stations are on different routes, the train you are taking will start or end at only one of them, so you won't have a choice regarding which station to alight at or embark from.
You can easily get connected buses or taxis which will take you to the destination of your choice.
Although there are metro stations serving the respective areas, there are no direct interchanges between railway and metro stations.
road: Hyderabad lies on the North-South Corridor, the national highway NH44 that runs from Srinagar to Kochi.
This highway is excellent, and will take you to Bengaluru, 560 km away, in hours.
It is 752 km from Chennai (using highways NH65 and NH16) and 800 km from Mumbai (NH65 till Pune and the expressway to Mumbai).

visakhapatnam.summary: Visakhapatnam (Telugu: విశాఖపట్నం Vishākhapaṭnam), popularly known as Vizag (vigh-ZAG), is the largest city in Andhra Pradesh.

air: 1 Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport (VTZ  IATA), Bhogapuram (50 km (31 mi) from central Vizag), ☏ +91 891 2851169.

Visakhapatnam has an excellent connectivity to Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Vijayawada, Tirupati, Delhi, Mumbai, Bhubaneswar, Kochi and Port Blair, as well as international destinations like Abu Dhabi and Singapore.
Sadly, the faraway airport lacks public transport, so taxis are your best bet to get into the city centre.
rail: 2 Visakhapatnam Junction  SCoR  (station code: VSKP).
Visakhapatnam is on the Kolkata–Chennai line and is connected to several cities of the country by rail.
All trains including fast expresses stop at the station.
road: Visakhapatnam is connected to Chennai and Kolkata via Bhubaneswar and Vijayawada by National Highway 16 (dual-carriageway, 120 km/h).
The Andhra Pradesh State Road Travel Corporation (APSRTC) runs buses from almost every city and town to Visakhapatnam, along with some private operators, who run buses from a few of the major cities.
Please check with APSRTC for timings.

araku valley.summary: Araku Valley (Telugu: అరకులోయ Arakulōya) is hill station in northern Andhra Pradesh, about 110 km (68 mi) from Visakhapatnam.
climate: November to February are the best months to visit and making an early reservation in the lodges is advisable as Araku Valley has few lodges and hotels.

rail: The Vizag to Araku train route is famous for its multiple tunnels passing through hills and forests.
A slow, passenger train leaves the Vizag station early in the morning (at 6:50AM), and the train ride is enjoyable.
The train runs through small mountains and over 40 tunnels, making it one of the most unique rail experiences in India.
road: There are buses that operate from APSRTC that have a daily tour as well as normal operations.
If you plan to visit Vanajagi and Lambasingi, the cost will be a bit higher than the base prices.

tirupati.summary: Tirupati (Telugu: తిరుపతి Tirupati, Tamil: திருபதி Tirupati) is the spiritual capital of Andhra Pradesh, India.

air: 1 Tirupati Airport (TIR  IATA, Renigunta Airport), Renigunta Airport Road, ☏ +91 877 227 5354.
This airport is a domestic airport.
It is possible to get connecting flights to and from Hyderabad and Chennai airport.
rail: This is a major railway station in the South-Central Railways system.
There are direct trains from nearby metro cities of Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad and others.
Trains can also be boarded at nearby cities - Renigunta (10 km from Tirupati) and Gudur (100 km).
road: National Highway NH 205 passes through Renigunta and hence is accessible from Chennai (3-4 hr), Bengaluru (at least 5 hours), Hyderabad (10-12 hours) and other nearby cities.
Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) - from Hyderabad or from within Andhra Pradesh
Tamil Nadu State Express Transport Corporation  (SETC) - from Chennai

andaman and nicobar islands.summary: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a group of nearly 600 islands in the Bay of Bengal.
climate: Mid-January to mid-May has the best weather, and often the best diving conditions.
The monsoon usually hits around late May and lasts until the end of July.
This is probably the worst time to visit the islands as there are strong winds, frequent rain and low visibility underwater.
From August to November there are some occasional showers and slightly rougher seas but diving can still be great during this period of the year.
The weather often takes a turn for the worse from the month of December to early January.
permits: Since 2018, most foreigners can visit 30 islands in the Andamans, including basically all of those commonly visited by tourists, without a Restricted Area Permit (RAP).
Citizens and former citizens of the aforementioned three countries must still obtain a RAP to visit any part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Indian nationals do not require a permit to visit the Andamans.

air: Application on an official form should be addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, South Andaman District, Port Blair.
The primary way to reach the Andaman and Nicobar Islands by air is from the Indian mainland to Port Blair.
The main airport of the islands is Veer Savarkar International Airport (IXZ IATA) in Port Blair.
sea: It's possible to take a ship from Kolkata (c.
60 hr), Chennai or Visakhapatnam (almost 4 days) to Port Blair.
Facilities are basic, though and many prefer to sleep on the deck rather than in the cramped bunks.

port blair.summary: Port Blair (officially Sri Vijaya Puram) is the capital and largest city of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands group, with a population of around 100,000.
closures: You can, however, do day trips to other places close by like Wandoor and Ross Island.

air: 1 Veer Savarkar International Airport (IXZ  IATA) (2 km (1.2 mi) from city centre).
A new modern terminal opened in 2024.
There are no night flights as the airport is handed over to the Indian Air Force after 15:00.
road: There are scheduled services to Havelock, Neil, Carnicobar, Hutbay, Campbellbay and other islands.
Buses connect Port Blair with other points on Grand Andaman, including Baratang Island (2½ hr), Rangat (6 hr) and Diglipur (8 hr).
To get "deluxe" bus tickets, go to the little arena of shops across the road from the bus station.
sea: Regular pax ship services are available to Port Blair from Chennai.
There are 3 to 4 sailings every month, The voyage takes about 50 to 60 hrs and the ship normally berths at Port Blair for about 2 to 4 days.
There are two jetties in Port Blair.

havelock island.summary: Havelock Island (Hindi: हैवलॉक द्वीप, Malayalam: ഹെയ്വ്ലോക് ദ്വീപുകള്‍), known officially as Swaraj Dweep (Island of Freedom), is the most visited of the Andaman Islands.
climate: Mid-January until mid-May sees the best weather, and often the best diving conditions.
The monsoon usually hits around late May, lasting until the end of July, and is probably the worst time to visit the island – strong winds, frequent rain and low visibility underwater.
August thru November see some occasional showers and slightly rougher seas, but diving can still be great at this time of year.
The weather often takes a turn for the worse for the month of December through early January.
Mosquitoes are a nuisance, particularly at dusk and after rain, and the Andaman Islands are malarial.
closures: While many of the lodges have 'resort' in their names, none come even close, thankfully.

air: 2-3 arrive daily from Port Blair (2-4 hours) and one from Rangat, one of which comes via Neil Island.
These ferries are air conditioned and can be booked in advance from the counter at the DSS in port Blair.

You can buy tickets yourself from the Port Blair ferry office on arrival, or resorts will often offer to pre-book your tickets for the journey there and back, which you can either picked up from a travel agency on Port Blair, or they will send someone to meet you prior to your ferry.
sea: Ferries are the major way on or off the island.
Schedules vary according to day and season, so enquiry locally, and see Andaman and Nicobar Islands about the differences between the ship types.
Government-operated ferries are best booked in advance, as seats often sell out.

neil island.summary: Neil Island, now known officially as Shaheed Dweep (Island of Martyrs), is in the Andaman Islands.

air: Ferry from Port Blair to Neil.
There's also the boat from Port Blair to Rangat which calls at Neil as its first stop.
sea: Neil Island has no ticket office, just get on the ferry and then buy your tickets on board.
The Rangat ferry calls at Havelock and then to Neil.

lakshadweep.summary: Lakshadweep, formerly the Laccadives, is a group of islands 200–440 km (120–270 mi) off India's southwestern coast in the Arabian Sea.
climate: Peak season is December to May, when it is cooler and drier.
May to September is the main (southwest) monsoon season, but the October–November northeast monsoon can also be rainy.
permits: Everybody, Indian or otherwise, requires a special permit to visit Lakshadweep.
The southernmost island of Minicoy in the Lakshadweep island group is now a permitted entry point.

air: Nearly everybody going to Lakshadweep has to pass through Kochi, from where you can continue by plane or ship.
1 Agatti Airport (AGX  IATA).
The only airport in Lakshadweep, with limited services from Kochi, Bengaluru and Goa on IndiGo, Fly91 and Alliance Air.
sea: The MV Tipu Sultan, MV Bharat Seema, MV Amindivi, MV Minicoy, MV Lakshadweep Sea, MV Arabian Sea and MV Kavaratti operate between Kochi in Kerala (Keralam) and various islands in Lakshadweep.
The trip takes 14–18 hours depending on the destination island.
The first four are basic 1960s-era ferries but fairly well maintained and tolerably comfortable and provides a comfortable journey.
